title: 《高等微積分》第 31 集｜微分學的起點與 ε-δ｜Loomis & Sternberg 第 3 章 §1
description:
本集是 Loomis 與 Sternberg《Advanced Calculus》第 3 章的開場（書頁 116）與第 1 節「實數上的複習」（書頁 117 到 120）。

第 3 章的主旨一句話講得完：微分學是「用線性映射去逼近非線性映射」的理論。前兩章已經把線性映射弄清楚了，現在要的是「逼近」這個詞的精確意思。

所以這一章從長度開始。要說一個逼近好不好，得先能量誤差有多大——誤差是一個向量，不是一個數。向量空間上量長度的東西叫範數。有了範數才能談切近，談完切近才能定義微分。整章的路線是：範數、連續、無窮小、微分與它的計算規則、方向導數與偏導數，最後在座標空間裡，微分就是一個偏導數排成的矩陣，叫 Jacobian 矩陣。章末的反函數定理與隱函數定理要用到實數的完備性，那要等到第 4 章。

第 1 節先回到實數上複習極限。定義是：f ( x ) 趨近 l，如果對每一個正的 ε 都存在一個正的 δ，使得 x 跟 a 的距離落在 0 與 δ 之間時，f ( x ) 跟 l 的距離就小於 ε。注意 x 等於 a 那一點被排除在外——微積分裡的差商在那一點根本沒定義，我們關心的正是它在附近的行為。

這個句子真正的開頭是三個量詞：對所有 ε、存在 δ、對所有 x。順序不能動；把「存在 δ」搬到「對所有 x」後面，就變成 δ 可以隨 x 改，那幾乎對每個函數都成立，等於什麼也沒說。

影片的 ε-δ 圖不是示意圖：畫的是 f ( x ) = x 平方在 a = 1，δ 由 |x 平方減 1| 等於 |x 減 1| 乘 |x 加 1| 這條界實際算出來（ε = 3/10 給 δ = 3/25，ε = 1/10 給 δ = 1/25），而且在區間上取樣驗過整段圖形真的沒有跑出 ε 帶。「ε 縮成三分之一，δ 也縮成三分之一」那一拍是兩張照著算出來的數字畫的圖。

接著是兩個典型用法。和的極限：把差拆成兩塊，每塊壓到 ε 的一半，兩個 δ 取小的那一個。倒數的極限比較有意思，因為分母裡有會動的 f ( x )：先花掉一個 δ 把 f 逼到 u 的一半以外，分母就有了下界，再估就穩了。

最後是實數的最小上界性質。它看起來平凡，卻是後面所有事情的地基——根號二就是「平方小於二的有理數」這個集合的最小上界，而有理數本身沒有這個性質。

下一集：範數。

title: Advanced Calculus, Episode 31 | Where the Calculus Starts, and Epsilon-Delta | Ch. 3, §1
description:
This episode covers the opening of chapter 3 (page 116) and section 1, the review in R (pages 117 to 120), of Loomis and Sternberg's Advanced Calculus.

The subject of chapter three fits in one sentence: the differential calculus is the theory of linear approximations to nonlinear mappings. The first two chapters settled what linear mappings are; what is needed now is a precise meaning for approximation.

So the chapter starts with length. To say an approximation is good you must measure how large the error is, and the error is a vector, not a number. What measures length on a vector space is a norm. Norms come first, then tangency, and only then can a differential be defined. The route runs: norms, continuity, infinitesimals, the differential and the rules for computing it, directional and partial derivatives, and finally, in a Cartesian space, the differential as a matrix of partial derivatives — the Jacobian matrix. The inverse-mapping and implicit-function theorems at the end of the chapter lean on completeness, which chapter four takes up.

Section one goes back to the real line. The definition: f of x approaches l if for every positive epsilon there is a positive delta such that whenever the distance from x to a lies strictly between zero and delta, the distance from f of x to l is less than epsilon. The point x equal to a is excluded, and not out of fussiness: the difference quotients of calculus are undefined there, and their behaviour nearby is exactly what matters.

The sentence really begins with three quantifiers: for every epsilon, there exists a delta, for every x. The order cannot move. Put the existence of delta after the quantifier on x and delta may depend on x, which holds for almost any function and therefore says nothing.

The epsilon-delta pictures are not sketches. They are drawn for f of x equal to x squared at a equal to one, with delta computed from the bound that the size of x squared minus one is the size of x minus one times the size of x plus one: epsilon three tenths gives delta three twenty-fifths, epsilon one tenth gives delta one twenty-fifth. The interval is then sampled to check that the graph really stays inside the epsilon band, so the beat where a narrower epsilon forces a narrower delta shows two pictures drawn from computed numbers.

Then the two typical uses. For a sum, split the difference in two, push each below half of epsilon, and take the smaller of the two deltas. For a reciprocal the denominator moves, so one delta is spent keeping f away from zero, which gives the denominator a floor and makes the estimate safe.

Finally the least upper bound property of the reals. It looks unremarkable and it is the foundation of what follows: the square root of two is the least upper bound of the rationals whose square is under two, and the rationals themselves do not have the property.

Next time: norms.

Part of a bilingual animated teaching series (English edition).
